on behalf of the uen group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the development of the union's internal market is essential for strengthening the links between the countries and citizens of the community. increasing cross-border exchanges of services in a competitive environment requires an increase in mutual trust, which should be supported by pro-consumer policies. this policy aims to improve the legal framework for crossborder services while simplifying procedures, which will increase competition, improve accessibility and improve service quality while reducing costs and benefiting european citizens. the report contributes to the improvement of this policy by pointing out a number of problems that are hampering the dynamic growth of the market, such as: the lack of a uniform system for regulating the obligations of cross-border service providers and the need to supplement eu documents in this field; the lack of clarity in the application of the rules, which creates mental barriers to foreign providers; the lower protection of the rights of service users compared to service providers; the lack of regulation of public and private services by the same rules; the divergence of the rules on the liability of cross-border service providers; the lack of transparency needed to protect these services. to improve consumer confidence, consideration should be given to the introduction of quality certificates for service providers. the conclusions and arguments in the report are consistent with the observations of the legal affairs committee. i thank the rapporteur for his detailed report.

in writing. i would like to thank mr lesse lehtinen for the substantive report. one of the four fundamental freedoms of the internal market is the freedom to provide services. over the years, the services sector has become increasingly important to the eu's economic and social development and has undergone a major transformation. despite the provisions of the ec treaty and the ongoing process of transposition of the services directive into national law, the free movement of services is hampered in practice by administrative rules and differences in the legal systems of the member states. in view of the challenges and threats posed by globalisation, as well as the shortcomings in the services sector identified in the report, it is essential to take action to remove obstacles to the provision of cross-border services. lack of consumer confidence and reluctance of firms to move outside their own country limits access to the internal market. community action should immediately put in place mechanisms to make it easier for businesses, in particular smes, and consumers to benefit from the internal market. it is therefore necessary to harmonise the rules on the provision of cross-border services and to introduce a minimum degree of harmonisation of quality requirements in order to protect the interests of users. strengthening cooperation between member states, reducing administrative procedures and adequately controlling services provided across borders is conducive to the growth of cross-border activities. harmonisation of quality requirements will strengthen consumer and supplier confidence in cross-border services. by facilitating the cross-border provision of services, a well-functioning single market for services will be created and thus the basis for an economically coherent internal market.

mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to stop this. in taking part in the debate on the impact of tax and customs policy on the implementation of the lisbon strategy, i would like to point out that some of the suggestions made in the report by mrs sahra wagenknecht on the tax systems of the member states will not have a positive impact on economic growth and employment in the countries of the european union. first, the prevention of tax competition and the attempt to harmonise corporate tax arrangements are contrary to the principle of the tax sovereignty of the member states of the european union. secondly, the reduction of corporate tax rates and the simultaneous abolition of corporate tax rebates not only do not reduce the budget revenues for this purpose, but on the contrary significantly increase them. this is confirmed by the example of my country, poland, where the corporate income tax rate has been significantly reduced and the revenue from this tax is higher year on year. thirdly, in this situation, i consider the suggestions in the report on coordination and tax systems, including direct taxes, to be dangerous and certainly not conducive to the objectives of the lisbon strategy.
mr. chairman, please! the main objective of the lisbon strategy is to increase the competitiveness of national economies. a high level of competitiveness helps to accelerate economic growth, create new jobs and finance important social objectives. unfortunately, the current tax system in the eu member states is not conducive to the implementation of the lisbon strategy. the tax burden on labour and business rights is too high, tax rates are too varied and the rules are too complex. at the same time, the tax system is overburdened with an excessive number of economic, fiscal, social and environmental functions and tasks. in order to be competitive, taxes must first create incentives for work, business development and innovation. to that end, taxes, especially direct taxes, should be set at a moderate level, avoiding unnecessary differentiation of rates and excessive progression. as direct taxes have a stronger negative impact on output and employment, more use should be made of indirect taxes in budgetary planning. as for the debate, mr president, i am concerned that there is too much ideology and politics and not enough real economic knowledge. the best example is the notions we use here, like fiscal dumping or social dumping. there is no objective standard of taxation and therefore no allegation of fiscal dumping can be made against those countries which impose low levels of taxation on companies.

mr. chairman, please! statistics show that in europe, about 30% of the population still reach for a cigarette every day. i agree wholeheartedly that non-smokers should be protected from the negative effects of inhaling nicotine smoke. i cannot, however, agree with the jacobin methods proposed in the resolution. we cannot create a repressive policy towards smokers, restricting their civil liberties. i think we should focus on broad public education, regulate retail prices by raising taxes, because scientific research shows that this is an effective weapon in the fight against tobacco addiction. the point that smoking should be banned in the workplace is uncontroversial. however, i think it should be extended to include a provision that ensures that each unit should provide employees with a space within which they can smoke without harming others. and in this day and age, creating a space like this doesn't have to be just a hollow, pointless manifestation of health promotion, but it has to be an effective action. i would like to take the opportunity to mention another problem that has its roots in the anti-smoking policies of many governments, namely the increase in the smuggling of counterfeit tobacco products, the main attraction of which is that they are cheaper than the original product. it is now one of the most lucrative sources of income for smugglers. remember, these products are sold in our stores, to our citizens. a seller who has taken up the sale of such a product will not hesitate to sell to a minor. so when we make policy on tobacco, we have to look at the problem from many perspectives. so that the legal reality we create is effective in helping to solve the problems associated with the use of nicotine products.

acting president of the council. madam president, commissioner, members and rapporteur, europe, africa and the world have changed a great deal in the last decade. europe is now a bloc of 27 member states with a confluence of sometimes very different foreign policy priorities and approaches. although it is not fair, in view of the volume of official development aid that europe provides for the african continent, to say that this continent has been neglected, it can, in our view, be said that there is a strategic gap in the relationship between europe and africa. in recent years the negative consequences of this vacuum have become more evident. the european union and its member states now understand the need to take relations with africa to a new level and the second eu-africa summit is the right moment to make that will clear. several reasons justify this new approach of recognising the importance of relations between the european union and africa: the widespread perception that the set of global challenges, such as peace and security or international trade, require concerted action by the international community and thus justify the emergence of new forms of cooperation; the search for answers to problems affecting both europe and africa, in particular the effects of climate change; the management of energy resources or migratory flows; africa's willingness to tackle common problems collectively and the need to adapt to changing geopolitical circumstances in the international context. the concrete expression of a new relationship between the union and africa is to be found in the documents which we hope will be adopted at the december summit: the joint strategy between the european union and africa, its first action plan and, we hope, the lisbon declaration. these documents reflect the specific nature of europe's relationship with africa, an approach which, on the one hand, favours multilateral channels and, on the other, seeks to address the various aspects of our relationship in an integrated manner. this approach is the difference the union can make, especially in comparison with other international actors. the treatment of africa as a strategic global partner is also reflected in the method used for preparing both the summit and the documents to be adopted. while the european union strategy for africa, adopted in 2005, is a union document that only binds the union, the strategy - for the first time a joint strategy - and the action plan are the result of joint work with the african side. the summit documents have been prepared by a joint group of experts since the beginning and we hope that they will be endorsed at the eu-africa ministerial troika meeting on 31 october, in a process in which non-state actors and civil society, both african and european, have been equally involved. the joint strategy and the first action plan are therefore the result of joint work, the present stage of drafting of which reflects and responds to many of the concerns and suggestions contained in the maria martens report, a report which is undoubtedly very complete and very comprehensive. it is emphasised that the partnerships between the european union and africa identified in both the joint strategy and the draft action plan address issues of common interest and are based on the fundamental criteria of adding value to existing cooperation and political dialogue and, in our view, having a positive impact on the daily lives of european and african citizens. the partnerships we want to build also seek to reflect a balance between the commitments made by both sides which will change the unilateral and aid-oriented logic of the relationship between the union and the acp. experience has also shown that political commitments require implementation and follow-up mechanisms to translate into more than just good intentions. between summits, in parallel with the regular meetings between the two committees and the ministerial troika, there is now the possibility of complementarity by sectoral ministerial meetings where appropriate. however, a real change in the relationship between the union and africa can only occur if there is also an effective ownership of the process by a number of other actors. in this regard, we want to establish joint informal expert groups for the implementation of each of the partnerships, open to the participation of a wide range of stakeholders: european and african parliaments, local authorities, african and european civil society, african sub-regional organisations, research institutions, specialised international organisations and institutions and the private sector. at the same time, efforts will be made to deepen cooperation and dialogue between the pan-african parliament and the pan-african parliament, also as channels for the implementation of the joint strategy and the action plan. although profound changes do not occur overnight, we are witnessing a moment of transformation in the relations between the two continents. the challenge is to be able to seize this opportunity and start implementing this new strategic vision for the euro-african dialogue. it is with this aim in mind that we are going to hold, with confidence and with the awareness that we are going to do what must be done, the next eu-africa summit in lisbon in december.

on behalf of the ppe-de group. - madam president! - i have to go. i'm not going to let you do this. a clear shortcoming of the current provisions on the law of enforcement is that the enforcement of a judicial order, once it has been declared enforceable in another member state, remains the exclusive domain of national law. under existing community legislation, it is not possible to obtain a freezing order that is enforceable throughout the european union. therefore, the establishment of a european account seizure order system, enabling the creditor to secure the amount due or the value of the claim by preventing the withdrawal or transfer of funds deposited in one or more bank accounts within the territory of the european union, seems to be a very appropriate and necessary solution. this system should be established by developing an additional, autonomous procedure which would run in parallel to national rules, subject to its being applicable only to cases of a cross-border nature. it should be noted that the order would have only a protective effect, i.e. it would result in the debtor's funds being blocked in the bank account without being transferred to the creditor's account. the court should certainly refrain from hearing or notifying the debtor before the seizure of his bank accounts is carried out, as this could have the opposite effect. the amount to be attached should be based on the amount of the claim lodged by the creditor, but it should be stressed that the debtor should have the right to appeal against the order issued and the competent authority for such an appeal should be the court which issued the order. at the same time, the criteria for determining the exemptions from enforcement should be set out in such a way as to enable the debtor to meet the basic needs of himself and his family. of course, further comparative analysis is needed at this stage, as many elements require further examination, but this does not change the fact that the introduction of a community legal procedure, such as a european account seizure order, aimed at facilitating and effective enforcement of monetary claims, would undoubtedly be a breakthrough in the shaping of the european judicial and economic area. in conclusion, i would like to congratulate mr lechner on his excellent, well-written report. we know very well how difficult it is to change community legislation, especially in this area.
on behalf of the uen group. - madam president! - i have to go. the green paper on improving the efficiency of judicial enforcement in the european union is the next step in the development of the european area of justice. i agree with the rapporteur's position in this report and support the introduction in the european union of a fast and efficient procedure for obtaining a bank account freezing order. in the context of the growing integration of the euro payments market, such a legal regulation seems both particularly necessary and reasonable. in view of the many risks involved in the pursuit of claims, i believe that the european union should introduce an autonomous additional procedure that would run parallel to national rules. it should apply only to cross-border cases and only to funds held in bank accounts and not to other assets. it is only a temporary security for the creditor's claims and not a final satisfaction. unjustified seizure can have serious consequences for the debtor, and can also have a negative impact on trust in the european legal order. i therefore believe that particular attention should be paid to the protection of the debtor, for example in the form of the lodging of a security by the creditor, the right to object, the limitation of the amount of enforcement or, finally, the obligation of the creditor to lodge a request for the opening of main proceedings within a specified period.
madam president! enforcement law is often referred to as the achilles' heel of european civil justice. no legislative proposal has been submitted so far on the actual means of enforcing judgments and the enforcement of a judicial order after its enforceability has been established in another member state remains the exclusive domain of national law. the current diversity of enforcement rules in the various member states of the european union makes it significantly more difficult to recover debts abroad. creditors seeking to enforce the order in another country face unfamiliar legal systems, procedural requirements and a language barrier that causes additional costs and delays in the enforcement procedure. the problems of debt collection in foreign countries constitute an obstacle to the free movement of payment orders within the union and to the proper functioning of the internal market. late and unrealised payments threaten the interests of both businesses and consumers. the commission's proposal to introduce a single european legal act, which would be autonomous and parallel to national legislation, therefore seems necessary, if not necessary. the legal basis for this document may be article 65 (c) of the treaty establishing the european community. therefore, in line with the green paper, a creditor should also be able to apply for a preservation order before the opening of the main proceedings. however, given the ad hoc nature of the procedure, the creditor should be required to demonstrate the existence of his claim and the urgency of the attachment order. unjustified occupation can have very serious consequences for the debtor, even depriving him of the basis for his existence. the debtor's right to object and the amount of the enforcement order are also important. it does not seem to be a good idea to set a uniform limit on the amount exempted from enforcement at the level of the european union. this decision should be left to the legislation of the debtor's country. in the case of service of preservation order on bank accounts, it is important to ensure that uniform standards are established in the european union for communication between courts and banks. it seems necessary to regulate the problem of debt recovery abroad by adopting a relevant legal act. however, it is also necessary to carry out a thorough analysis of the regulations already in force in the various community countries and to consider the effectiveness of alternatives to european rules. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr lechner, on a very well-prepared and balanced report.
madam president! the problem of the effective enforcement of monetary claims within the european union is of great importance for the proper functioning of the internal market. community action in this area should be considered. one of the most interesting sayings i've heard in my law practice is, "when you do a favor for someone, you become their debtor". sometimes it's true. late and unrealised payments threaten the interests of both businesses and consumers. the differences in the efficiency of debt collection that we currently see in the european union can distort competition among firms operating beyond the territory of a member state. enforcement systems vary from country to country. in some cases, they're effective, in others, they're less so. at present, we can see that debtors have the possibility to transfer funds almost immediately from accounts known to the creditor to other accounts in the same or another member state. this makes it impossible for creditors to block these funds. in addition, creditors seeking enforcement in another member state face unfamiliar legal systems and procedural requirements. the language barrier and the cost of the proceedings are also important. i therefore believe that the proposal to create a european system for the seizure of bank accounts should be welcomed. given the increasing integration of the euro payments business, such a legal regulation seems necessary and reasonable. i congratulate mr lechner on this report and i think it will be a very important legal event for the european union.

madam president! the framework directive on soil protection will, in my view, be an instrument to ensure food production and sufficient clean water for the next generations of european union citizens. soil also has many other important functions: it provides the basis for human activities, including cities and infrastructure, as well as for nature and precious landscapes. finally, soil protection is essential to preserve our natural heritage and natural resources. in this situation, a flexible framework directive recognising the principle of subsidiarity will be an instrument to encourage member states to protect their soils. a directive thus drafted is binding on the member states as regards the results to be achieved in the field of soil protection, but leaves the choice of the forms and methods of such protection to the member states. the proposal in the directive to make publicly available and update every five years lists of contaminated sites, including regional lists, by member states is noteworthy. this is important information for the protection of the health and life of the citizens of the european union.
member of the commission. mr president, first of all i would like to thank the speakers in this debate for their positive contributions and i would like to outline the commission’s view on a number of key issues raised by parliament. let me state that the commission will follow the development of its proposal in the council and in parliament and consider its position under the light of these developments. i will start with those aspects of the thematic strategy which appear in the report of the committee on the environment and which are not covered in the directive. i welcome the support given in the report to tackling soil protection at a european level and the crucial links between soil protection and any strategy to combat climate change, biodiversity loss and desertification. i also agree on the fact of reviewing existing environmental legislation to fully exploit and further strengthen the potential synergies with soil protection. finally, the resolution you have approved proposes a number of recommendations as regards a new directive on biowaste and a communication on desertification. the commission will take these recommendations into account when developing further measures implementing the thematic strategy. let me now turn to the soil framework directive and outline the commission’s current thinking regarding the issues raised. many of the amendments proposed by the committee on the environment provide useful clarifications to the proposal. i am referring in particular to a better clarification of the objective of the legislation and the role played by soil functions in ensuring sustainable use of soil in article 1, pursuant to amendment 36. in addition, elements such as the introduction of voluntary codes of good practice or of a non-binding annex on possible measures to combat soil degradation can be supported in articles 4 and 8, pursuant in part to amendments 58 and 65.the addition of acidification to the list of soil degradation processes that need to be tackled in order to consider the different soil conditions that apply in some new member states. the commission also considers the clarification introduced in the provision dealing with the identification of contaminated sites in article 10, pursuant to amendment 74, as an improvement to the text. however, there are also a number of amendments which raise concerns for the commission. firstly, amendment 38 on article 1, to make the soil framework directive subsidiary to other european union legislation so that soil protection provisions contained in other community legislation would take precedence over the provisions of this directive. secondly, it is clear that there must be a date by which the programmes of measures for tackling agricultural threats should be drawn up. thirdly, some amendments, such as amendment 77 concerning article 12, eliminate the provisions concerning the information on soil contamination to be provided for certain land transactions. the soil status report is a very important part of the commission’s proposal. it will increase the level of transparency in land transactions, assist the competent authorities in identifying contaminated sites and speed up the establishment of the inventory. the costs involved in producing this report are negligible compared to the amounts of land transactions of such industrial sites. i would like to emphasise the importance of keeping a common list of activities in annex 2. this annex is of fundamental importance if a meaningful, enforceable, systematic and cost-effective inventory of contaminated sites is to be achieved. many member states and regions already use a very similar list to carry out their investigations. it is very important to have a common list to ensure harmonised implementation and to avoid a distortion of the internal market for the different sectors. thus we will provide investors, economic operators, public authorities and society at large with legal certainty and a common ground to assess the progress in identifying contaminated sites. i shall provide a complete list of the commission’s current position on the amendments to parliament’s mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to stop this. thank you to all the reporters. we're facing a complex problem here. on the one hand, there are the environmental aspects of our atmosphere, and on the other hand, there is the development of air transport, which is an important economic activity, which includes transport, tourism, which is carried out in a highly competitive market. the decisions in this area should be prudent and clear, but should in no way discriminate against european carriers, including those from the new member states. the european aviation industry can be seriously harmed without reducing harmful gas emissions. it is obvious that the earth's atmosphere knows no boundaries. the inclusion of carbon dioxide emissions from civil aviation in the union scheme should therefore be considered appropriate. i also think that we should also take into account the emission of other gases, such as toxic nitrogen oxides. i consider that the most important measures are those which will effectively reduce harmful gas emissions, inter alia, through the use of innovative solutions in the field of aircraft engines, the design of aircraft with better aerodynamic parameters, and radical improvements in air traffic management, which will reduce unnecessary time in the air. i'm considering emissions trading as a substitute right now. i would consider it reasonable today to adopt the base period 2007-2009, to set the emission ceiling at a level of 5 to 10% higher than 100% due to the growing interest in aviation and to include also non-eu carriers operating in the union.
mr. chairman, please! we are discussing today a proposal to integrate european civil aviation into the eu's emissions trading system. in my view, this very important project was prepared in haste, without proper consultation of the aviation industry, especially from the new member states, and without analysing the economic and social consequences of its implementation, as well as the environmental consequences for civil aviation and the risks to europe's economic development, for example in the area of tourism, which is the main source of income for many regions. the project also threatens the competitiveness of airlines and could contribute to a radical deterioration of the already difficult financial situation of many european airlines. therefore, i consider that the earliest possible date for the start of the system, taking into account the aviation sector, for all connections is 2012. i strongly support the so-called wide geographical coverage of the system, i.e. covering all flights to and from the union regardless of the nationality of the carrier. only this solution guarantees the desired environmental impact and does not expose european carriers to a drastic reduction in their competitiveness. i believe that the total number of allowances allocated to the aviation sector should be determined at community level by reference to the average aviation emissions from at least 2005 to 2007, and that the emission limit should be set at 100%. given the divergent views that have been presented during our discussion and the fact that this project affects both the environment and the economy of all the eu countries and our citizens, we should make decisions that are balanced and good.

president of the commission. mr president, i should like to thank all the groups for their very interesting and challenging comments. let me first try to answer some specific issues, and then i shall make some general comments. i should like to thank mr nassauer for the general support he gave to our priorities. regarding the main issue – subsidiarity – he mentioned, let me say that we are as committed as he to the goal he has set, more precisely: to create a new culture of subsidiarity in europe and to give our own example. i really am committed to that. i am not pretending that we are perfect. sometimes it is difficult to change old habits, but we are moving in the right direction. when there are mistakes, which sometimes happens, then we try to correct them. the recent case we mentioned regarding the apfelwein is a good example of that, and we should accept that sometimes we cannot foresee all the consequences of the regulations we are preparing. i want to assure you that i and the college that is present here are committed to subsidiarity. in all our initiatives we are now looking at the need for a specific legislative initiative – the impact assessment and the quality of our proposals – and we try to do it that way. let me just highlight that, out of the 26 strategic initiatives i have announced, only 8 are of a legislative nature; out of 61 priority initiatives, only 28 are of a legislative nature; out of 87, only 36 are of a legislative nature in general. on top of this, we will withdraw 30 pieces of legislation. however, the point i want to make to you is the following: when we speak about the new culture of subsidiarity, i need your help to explain to our citizens that this is in order to strengthen the european union, not to weaken it; in order to make the institutions more democratic and more accountable, and not to give in to those who are attacking europe and the european union in a populist, demagogic way. this is not the way i see subsidiarity. sometimes, in some of our member states, people say that, because of subsidiarity, the commission or the european parliament should not come forward with this kind of programme because this goes against subsidiarity. in fact, if what they do not want is the european union to act when european action is needed, then i do not agree that this is indeed in favour of subsidiarity. to give you a recent example: in march the european council adopted, as you know, some very important ideas for energy and the environment, namely protection against climate change. for instance, we adopted the general principles of unbundling. this was a decision of the european council. however, i have sometimes heard some member states state that the commission should not insist on unbundling, because this is against the principle of subsidiarity. i do not agree with this, and i have to say so. it is, in fact, resistance to an important european movement that is in favour of creating a real internal market for energy and of having a very strong policy against climate change. this is not in favour of subsidiarity. this is the point where we need your help. we need your help to explain when the european union action is needed, and to be critical of us when you think that european action is not needed, so that we should, if necessary, scrap some legislation. i will come back to mr swoboda’s point on communication later, but i think he is right. in fact, i, together with vice-president wallström and the whole college, are working on this. but the basic idea is, precisely, partnerships. let us be honest about this. we cannot do everything by ourselves. when i say ‘we’, i mean the european institutions – the commission and the european parliament. we need the active involvement of leaders at all levels – national and regional. this is important for subsidiarity. for instance, the länder in germany, the regions in most of our member states, are critically important, and my college and i have been all over europe in the national parliaments, sometimes in the different regions, explaining. i was recently in poland, saying this very clearly, saying that europe is not them in brussels or strasbourg: europe is us, all over europe, and this is a collective responsibility. that is, once again, a change of paradigm, because if you want to motivate the citizens for the european idea, we have to share with them those priorities and not just think about ‘some people in brussels or in strasbourg’ telling the other citizens what they should or should not do. we have mentioned the social dimension. i could not, of course, highlight all the points. let me just tell you that in our programme there are many legislative and non-legislative initiatives in this area. most importantly, we will conclude the work on stock-taking of european society with the vision of how to promote opportunities, access and solidarity in the europe of the 21st century. this will pave the way for a new social agenda and provide the framework for a dynamic and modern approach to the contribution of european union policy to european society today. the commission will also submit proposals to amend the european works council directive in order for them to anticipate and accompany restructuring. another piece of legislation will concern the conditions of pregnant women, aiming at improving existing maternity protection provisions with a view to reconciling professional, private and family life. an initiative will concern the deepening of the open method of coordination in the areas of social protection and social inclusion. this will be accompanied by a recommendation on active inclusion of people furthest from the labour market, concentrating on three pillars: job opportunities and vocational training, income support, and better access to quality services. this takes place in the context of the overall lisbon strategy for growth and jobs. finally, the commission will adopt the communication on anticipating and managing change, launching the second phase of consultation of european social partners on anticipating company restructuring. just to give you some examples that we are indeed committed to the social agenda in europe. mr duff, as regards the need to ratify the treaty, as you understand, i fully share that priority, and i think, precisely, that the social and cultural dimension of europe should be highlighted. i am doing my best in this matter, trying to explain that in europe we need a strong internal market, but europe is more than a market, and i think you can agree that this is also a shared commitment. regarding the ‘wise men’s group’ proposal of president sarkozy, about which you have asked for my opinion, the commission has discussed this issue. we are, naturally, in favour of any initiative that promotes debate and reflection on the future of europe. as real democrats we like debate. that is perhaps our tropisme, but we like debate, we like ideas and the exchange of ideas. so i think that president sarkozy’s initiative should be seen as part of the promotion of such debate and reflection. however, the commission is keen to make sure that this initiative, if it were to be approved by the european council, does not undermine our efforts to build on the success of the lisbon treaty and, most of all, does not undermine its certification. we must be clear about this. that is why we think that this group, in the event of approval by the european council, should not engage in a new institutional in writing. the rapporteur, mr thierry cornillet, rightly stressed that the community and the member states should deepen the discussion on the political strategy for humanitarian action in the relevant council forum by setting up a new ad hoc working group. indeed, the establishment of such a group (e.g. cohuma, i.e. the joint working group on humanitarian aid) would allow the development of coherent methods to enable rapid and consistent action in this field. it was also rightly noted that the frequency of natural disasters has increased and their effects are becoming more significant, which results in the need to strengthen intervention. so i agree with the proposal that the eu should increase its ability to react quickly. the readiness and response capacity will indeed be achieved through improved coordination, early warning mechanisms and adequate international storage of materials and supplies.
mr. chairman, please! i am convinced that the regulations we have adopted are very necessary and will contribute to improving the environment and human health. soil is a limited and hard-to-renew natural resource. it deserves special protection because of its social, economic, environmental and cultural functions. i share the view that soil protection should be regulated at community level in order to guarantee a minimum level of soil protection in all the member states of the union. i welcome the proposal to create publicly available national lists of contaminated sites. an inventory of sites where soil contamination may have occurred in the past shall be carried out. the principle of subsidiarity should be applied to assist the member states of the union in the reclamation of contaminated land and to promote the removal of dangerous substances that remain on it. the introduction of appropriate regulations to limit soil degradation, ensure its sustainable use and at the same time allow the reuse of degraded land is a clear step forward in the protection of environmental resources. i therefore consider it particularly important to achieve the harmonisation of the laws of the member states on soil protection.
mr. chairman, please! i voted for the directive. compliance with the directive will allow degraded land to be put into use, while protecting green land from being used for industrial and commercial purposes. this directive will also allow the classification of soils in terms of their assessment for crop and livestock production, with particular reference to the production of high-quality food. i would like to stress the need for a european strategy to identify and address soil degradation problems. the great diversity of soil types means that, apart from national action, a european strategy is needed, based on prevention, raising public awareness of the need to protect soils and identifying risk areas to address this problem at european level.
in writing. the proposed framework directive consolidates the legal solutions for soil protection policy that are fragmented in other legal acts on waste management, pesticide use and environmental protection. the document proposes not only measures to protect and sustainably use soil to prevent its degradation due to climate change, but also measures to restore already degraded soils. the instrument of the framework directive will first of all allow for the diversity of soils in the various eu countries to be taken into account and will guarantee flexibility in its implementation. its objectives are already being achieved, to varying degrees, on the basis of legislation in the member states. on the other hand, the directive represents a huge opportunity for countries that have not had soil protection regulations in place until now. in this respect, the decisions to introduce a definition of contaminated sites and to require eu countries to draw up national lists of such sites, which are made public and reviewed every five years, seem to be important. in addition, they welcome the provision for the obligation to draw up a recovery strategy within seven years of the entry into force of the directive, taking into account the objectives of the remedial actions and the financing mechanism and identifying priority areas requiring special protection against erosion, salinity or acidification. thank you for your attention.
in writing. mr. chairman, please! the commission's proposal to the european parliament is based on the new comitology procedure, which significantly increases the powers of the european parliament - the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. the rapporteur believes that the new procedure applies to issues covered by the prospectus rules, such as measures relating to the exemption from the obligation to publish a prospectus, the format of the prospectus and equivalence with regard to third countries, and this is to be welcomed. the amendments tabled on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs in the plenary vote are based on this conviction. the report provides additional reflection on the significant progress made in harmonising the rules of european financial and stock exchange markets. this is largely the result of the inevitable process of globalisation, but also partly due to the financial services action plan of 1999. the choice made at the beginning of the 1990s in countries such as poland, where the capital market was rebuilt on the basis of european standards, is also valid, and this now facilitates the harmonisation of rules at european union level.

acting president of the council. mr president, madam president, the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, or cites, provides the international legal framework for the conservation of tigers and other endangered species. the communities and their member states are strong supporters of cites, both politically and financially. in recent years, the community has particularly stressed the need for greater focus on the effective implementation of cites controls in order to reduce illegal slaughter and trade and to ensure sustainable trade in species. to underline this need, commission recommendation no 207/425/ec of 13 july 2007 was published, which identifies a set of actions to monitor the application of council regulation no 338/97 on the protection of species of wild fauna and flora by regulating trade therein. moreover, the species 'panttera tigris' is listed in annex a to commission regulation (ec) no 1332/2005 of 9 august 2005, in addition to being listed in annex i to the cites convention, and as such any possibility of moving specimens of that species is only exceptional and subject to strict criteria. the committee stresses that these criteria and any decision to authorise trade must take into account the fact that this activity does not adversely affect the conservation status of the species. we also stress the need for international cooperation and in particular capacity building to facilitate the implementation of policies for the conservation and sustainable use of wild fauna and flora in the states of the species' range. the union thus supported the decisions on asian big cats adopted at the 14th meeting of the parties to cites earlier this year, with a view to intensifying enforcement and conservation efforts. we are also prepared to assist india and the other states in the distribution area in implementing these decisions. we recognise that effective implementation of conservation measures requires the participation of local populations. through cites we have stressed the need to ensure the support and cooperation of local and rural communities in managing wild fauna and flora resources and, consequently, in combating illegal trade.

mr. chairman, please! any attempt to rationalize the community's reality must be respected, especially since it concerns the employment problem, which is perhaps the most sensitive aspect of the socioeconomic transformation of an integrated europe. the rapporteur is very good at finding the atmosphere of particular expectation that accompanies this legislative initiative by giving the report an accessible, really interesting form. the regulation of the european parliament and of the council replaces the current practice of collecting data on job vacancies under a gentlemen's agreement with a decision establishing a legal framework for this activity. the opportunity is there to improve the next stage of the information commitment process of integration, notably as part of the basic european economic indicators. this has created a much-needed legal framework to support the development of the necessary methodological foundations for the summaries of the growing data sets. the regulation also offers other benefits. it allows for higher standards of quality and comparability of statistics. it also facilitates the formulation of effective labour market policies based on relevant data in both the national and international context. it will also allow the implementation of these issues in individual countries to be monitored. the governments of the new eu countries agree that quarterly statistics will provide them with a coherent system of indicators for assessing the labour market. they note, by the way - and we add with relief - that the introduction of this regulation will not increase the need for funds for the implementation of quarterly surveys. in justifying its position on this project, the polish government stresses that the standardisation of research at european level and the monitoring of its quality should contribute to the expansion of knowledge on the development of demand for specific qualifications and to a more effective monitoring of the situation on the polish labour market. it will also help to formulate employment and wage forecasts more accurately. the comparability of data at european level will allow the extent of mismatches in national labour markets to be assessed against the rest of the union. it also has practical implications for the correlation between employment policy and supply and for the planning of future workers' vocational training.
mr. chairman, please! i would like to express my support for the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on quarterly job vacancy statistics in the community. it is not debatable how important it is that these data are collected systematically and in a uniform manner, while meeting the standards set in all member states. the value of the information thus collected is undeniable in the context of the assessment of the conditions prevailing in the labour market in the european union, as well as for the functioning of the european central bank. the current situation where data is collected on the basis of an unwritten contract clearly shows that this is an inefficient solution and that it is necessary to change it. only if a regulation is adopted which establishes uniform rules for the production of high-quality statistics throughout the community will it be possible to have a precise overview and analysis of the factors which constitute the overall picture and the state of the labour market. this regulation will not only oblige member states to produce statistics according to precisely defined standards, but will help them do so by providing a ready-made tool. the harmonisation of such research at european level will contribute to a better understanding of the development of demand for specific occupations in national markets and will allow for more accurate employment and wage forecasts. it is therefore essential that a legal instrument which will define in a clear and transparent manner all the rules for the collection of data on job vacancies covering the whole community should enter into force.
mr. chairman, please! in response to the commission's recommendation on cross-border collective management of copyright in respect of legal online music services, parliament adopted a resolution calling for a framework directive to regulate this issue. the commission failed to carry out the necessary and extensive consultation of the interested parties, including parliament, in breach of democratic procedures. it is unacceptable to ignore the institutional triangle and to apply the so-called soft law approach without prior consultation and formal involvement of parliament and the council. that recommendation, which in practice aims to give rightholders greater freedom to choose their collective management organisation as appropriate, has in fact far-reaching consequences for the copyright and related rights market, posing a potential threat not only to competition rules but also to cultural diversity. as a consequence, market power will be concentrated in the hands of a few of the largest entities, which will be able to circumvent the network of bilateral agreements and license the entire european market. it is worth recalling that around 5 to 7% of the eu's gdp comes from trade in goods or services protected by copyright and related rights. this is all the more indicative of the importance of properly managing and strengthening the rights concerned in the digital age. in compliance with the principles of competitiveness, it is necessary to prevent the compression of creators' revenues, while ensuring that users of musical works are granted a community-wide licence that is appropriate to the business model of the future. to that end, the commission should submit a draft appropriate legally binding instrument to the actors in this field as soon as possible.
member of the commission. madam president, honourable members, ladies and gentlemen, since july 2007, the commission and the portuguese presidency of the european union have been working closely together to launch the process of developing a more strategic and effective response by the european union to situations of fragility in partner countries. this process will have to be continued in the framework of future presidencies. the aim is not to label or classify countries, but to adapt their instruments and responses to specific situations. in these fragile situations, major obstacles to poverty reduction exist. institutional capacity is very limited, with states unable to assume the functions of a king or the consequences of natural disasters or violent conflicts or the lack of political will of the government to achieve development goals. in extreme cases, these situations can have consequences beyond national borders and affect regional stability and even global security. the idea of fragility is not new, even if the international debate is relatively recent. donors, partner countries and civil society have long recognised the need to be more effective in particularly unfavourable situations in order to achieve sustainable development goals. each situation is complex and different and requires an appropriate response, involving both diplomatic action, humanitarian aid, development cooperation and security and crisis management interventions. the effectiveness of the eu response requires a long-term commitment, but also the definition of clear objectives when engaging in a fragile country. the main focus will remain on capacity development and human security, with a view to sustainable development and poverty reduction. however, it should be avoided that support for fragile situations is at the expense of the stronger countries. commitments to increase aid are thus back in the foreground. the european commission presented a communication proposing a pragmatic approach to the european union's engagement in challenging environments for sustainable development, stability and peace. this communication was forwarded to all the institutions of the european union. the general affairs council on 19 and 20 november will adopt the conclusions in this field. it will invite the commission to develop a concrete work plan for the implementation of the recommendations and priority actions set out in the communication, which aim to address fragility more effectively by supporting the efforts of partner countries to create or restore the conditions necessary for their sustainable development. the year 2008 will be devoted to preparing this strategic approach of the european union to situations of fragility. this process requires the active participation of all eu institutions and all development actors in the eu and in partner countries. the european parliament's contribution to this exercise is of great interest to the commission, which invites it to be actively involved in this debate, which should make it possible to support a comprehensive strategy to respond to situations of fragility and thus contribute to the creation of the right conditions for sustainable development, stability, peace and democratic governance.

on behalf of the uen group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the amendment of the community railway safety directive should support efforts to establish a common market for rail transport services. hence the need to establish a common framework for railway safety. the commission should be empowered to adapt and adopt common security measures and common security objectives. and also to introduce a uniform certification system. to achieve this, it is first necessary to check the existing requirements and the safety situation in the member states and to ensure that the current level of safety of the rail system is not reduced in any country. it is also necessary to identify priority areas where safety needs to be further improved. the safety certificate is intended to provide evidence that the railway undertaking has established a safety management system to oversee the provision of transport services on the european network. rolling stock authorised for placing in service in one member state must be so authorised in other member states, provided that, of course, the requirement to have such authorisation is applicable in the member state concerned. every time a rolling stock is put into service, a legal entity responsible for its maintenance is to be designated, which is what this directive says and which is very important. such entity may be the railway undertaking, the subcontractor or the vehicle owner. and that's what the service market is looking for. this initiative will make rail transport more competitive and will help to preserve jobs in the sector. the amendment of this directive is highly anticipated, especially for the new member states. i therefore congratulate the rapporteur.
mr. chairman, please! the changing conditions in which the economy operates require continuous changes, inter alia, in railway operations, including in the field of railway safety. hence the need to adapt the rules to life. changes such as the enlargement of the schengen area to include a number of countries with different technical railway equipment, the abolition of railway monopolies in a number of countries, the creation of network operators and transport companies of regional and international importance require clear clarification of concepts and principles of conduct relating to ensuring safety within the union. this will allow for a broad alignment of national legislation. in this respect, the proposals contained in mr costa's report are an added value. the simplification changes proposed by mr costa, such as the transfer of article 14 of annex vii to the interoperability directive, significantly improve the readability of the directive. it is appropriate to establish a more transparent responsibility for safety. i would like to thank mr paolo costa for his contribution to the report.
on behalf of the uen group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the amendments to the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the coordination of laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the pursuit of television broadcasting activities are intended to ensure that providers of on-demand audiovisual media services in the member states can fully benefit from the internal market by applying the principle of country-of-origin regulation. the amendment of the directive opens up the current european union legislation to the latest technological advances. the european commission proposal differentiates between linear services, i.e. transmission via traditional television, the internet or mobile television, which continuously transmit content to the viewer according to a fixed schedule, and non-linear services similar to television, which are downloaded from the network on demand. maintaining the 'television without frontiers' directive in its current form would exacerbate unjustified differences in the regulatory treatment of different forms of distribution of identical or similar media content. the current rules on television should continue to apply to linear services, while for non-linear services, minimum, basic rules should be established, for example on the protection of minors, the prohibition of incitement to racial hatred or the prevention of crypto-advertising. the proposed amendment takes these conditions into account and the uen political group will therefore vote in favour of the proposal.

vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your report. guns are not ordinary products. tragic events, whether in erfurt, antwerp or helsinki, have made us aware of the potential danger posed by weapons to the safety of our citizens and especially to children. our requirements for the production, sale and possession of weapons must therefore be strict. although our european law expressly allows member states to go beyond the commonly agreed level of protection, i am very grateful that parliament is seeking to significantly strengthen the security situation as far as weapons in europe are concerned. i would like to thank in particular the rapporteur for the committee on the internal market and consumer protection, mrs kallenbach, and the chairman of that committee, mrs mccarthy. i would like to thank you both very much for your excellent cooperation. i would like to recall the background to today's decision. the starting point was the necessary change in our law to make it possible to ratify the un arms protocol. it was only after that that a comprehensive change in european gun laws was planned. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the negotiations, but that it should be involved in the negotiations. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject. we do not attack the different traditions and cultural circumstances in our member states, but respect the fact that there are long and very different traditions concerning hunters, sports shooters and gun collectors. a european firearms passport will soon facilitate cross-border travel and provide a secure basis for cross-border encounters between hunters and marksmen. we have also decided to ensure that weapons are properly labelled and registered, so that crossborder trade and transport of weapons in the internal market is possible, but also traceable and therefore safer. an important innovation is the registration of all weapons in personal possession. we need to know who has what weapons. with this report, we are putting an additional bar on the illegal possession of or trade in arms. the data will be kept for 20 years to ensure the traceability of weapons for a sufficient period. that is in every respect welcome. however, the commission considers it appropriate at this point to clarify in a statement our understanding of the new recital 9e to the data protection directive. we have also decided that the acquisition of weapons by minors under 18 years of age should be prohibited in future. europe is sending a clear message: guns are not for young people! of course, the fact remains that sports shooters and hunters, even if they are not yet 18 years old, can pursue their hobby, but only under the supervision of adults, such as coaches or parents. too much bad luck has happened with guns in the hands of teenagers. i hope that the new regulation will help to avoid further accidents and raise awareness of the need to handle weapons with special care, especially among young sports shooters or hunters. we were faced with the fact that technology and criminal energy in europe had led to a problem that had never been seen before: i mean the conversion of weapons that are not dangerous in themselves into sharp weapons. mrs mccarthy was the first to draw attention to this problem. in fact, it was a simple circumvention of the law. but that's over now, too. we will have to deal even more intensively with the problem of firearms reproductions in the next two years, in order to avoid any security gaps. the same is true of the question of how to disarm firearms in the most effective way. you also know that the commission has advocated the introduction of sanctions in european law, since the european court of justice has clearly ruled on this issue. the commission acknowledges, however, that there is a reference to these criminal sanctions and to the un protocol in recital 8. this is important because compliance with article 5 of the un protocol necessarily requires sanctions by member states. i am confident that the member states will also provide for this in their national legislation. a commission statement on this subject is also available in the secretariat-general of the parliament (see 'commission statement appended to debate'). i should like to take this opportunity to thank mr alvaro in particular for his support. europe is giving itself a modern right to bear arms. the european parliament has always been a party to the treaty of rome, and it has always been a party to the treaty of rome. we are raising our common european protection requirements. it is now up to the member states to recognize the signs of the times and to develop the rules in detail in accordance with their own national conditions. so if anyone thinks that stricter rules are right and necessary at national level, he has my full personal support and i can only urge him to do so! i am counting on your colleagues in the national parliaments to make a clear decision on arms. it's always got to be, "stay ahead of the curve". today's decision paves the way for this and i thank you for it. commission declarations appended to debate the commission welcomes the rapid adoption of the council directive amending directive 91/477 on the control of the acquisition and possession of weapons, but regrets that the council opposed its initial proposal on article 16 on criminal sanctions. the commission notes that the community has competence to establish criminal sanctions in accordance with article 5 of the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, supplementing the united nations convention against transnational organized crime. accordingly, the commission considers that any decision to ratify the protocol would have to be accompanied by a declaration of competence which correctly reflects the scope of the community's competence. the commission reserves its institutional rights in this regard.' 2) draft declaration on data protection the commission notes that the processing of personal data under this directive is subject to compliance with directive 95/46/ec and cannot prejudice the level of protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data under the provisions of community and national law, and in particular does not alter the obligations and rights set out in directive 95/46/ec. in this respect, the need to extend the minimum period during which the registers containing information on the owners of weapons are kept from ten to twenty years should be justified. the commission is convinced that such processing of personal data is justified in view of both the dangerous nature and longevity of such weapons and their possible misuse for criminal purposes, which therefore requires the proper tracing of both firearms and their owners. the commission further notes that, in view of the purposes of this directive, and in accordance with the requirements of directive 95/46/ec, access to the centralised data filing system, or the system guaranteeing access to non-centralised filing systems, should only be available to police and judicial authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences.'

mr. chairman, please! the european parliament and council directive on clean air quality is of great importance for the health of europe's citizens, especially since substances emitted by industry, transport and power plants can be transported over long distances, such as pollen and sulphur, nitrogen and lead oxides. the directive sets emission limits for these pollutants and emphasises the principle of reducing emissions at source. however, the conditions for meeting these requirements are different. in zones and agglomerations with a high number of polluting entities, such as coal-fired furnaces, plants with old technologies, it takes time and a lot of money to comply with the requirements of the directive. therefore, in justified cases, in accordance with amendment no 2, the deadline for the introduction of the requirements of the directive should be postponed. the directive rightly emphasises the need to monitor pollutant emissions, which is of great importance in reducing pollution, including transboundary pollution. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr krahmer.
member of the commission. mr president, a number of key elements have been included in the overall compromise package that is now proposed. most importantly, it contains the following elements:- the time extension option for pm10 is kept at the level of the common position; there can be no delay in taking the measures and a single step approach will reduce the administrative burden;- standards for particulate matter pm10 are unchanged in accordance with the original commission proposal;- a realistic and timely annual pm2.5 target and a limit value set at 25 µg per cubic metre to be achieved at 2010 and 2015 respectively;- an indicative limit value for 2020 that adds to the ambitious pm2.5 agenda for the mandatory review in 2013;- a legally binding exposure concentration obligation in 2015 that complements the exposure reduction target in triggering prompt measures that are expected to provide the maximum public health benefit; and- a commission declaration on the progress in developing the community measures at source. the new recital 15 also strengthens the determination of the two co-legislators to consider as a matter of priority the legislative proposals put forward by the commission to address emission at source at community level. i know that these elements were all-important to parliament at first reading and in the committee this time round. i believe that the proposed current compromise will satisfy parliament as important ground was won on the key principle of the ambitious yet realistic ambient air quality standard setting, with a clear roadmap including the adoption of the necessary community measures and a well-defined review in 2013. i am also particularly pleased to note the importance given by both parliament and the council to finding a compromise in this directive. the resulting compromise, as well as the demonstrated resolve, enables the european union to take the effective next steps in ensuring healthier air for its citizens. to conclude, the commission is very pleased with the outcome of the negotiations. it can accept the proposed compromise amendments in full. i wish to thank and to congratulate, once more, the rapporteur, mr krahmer, for all his efforts to reach an agreement at second reading.

member of the commission. madam president, i wish to begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr golik, for his excellent report on the commission proposal for a single council regulation for the promotion of agricultural products on the internal as well as the external markets. the aim of the present proposal is to merge two existing council regulations on internal and external promotion into one single regulation. the overall goal of this exercise is totally in line with our simplification exercise and is intended to increase the transparency of the european union’s promotion scheme for agricultural products. the objective is not to fundamentally change the information and promotion policies. the amendments proposed by mr golik and his colleagues address several important issues regarding the eu promotion scheme, such as, firstly, more importance and a larger budget for promotion programmes in third countries; secondly, a higher community share of promotion measures and, thirdly, a lower share of financial contribution by the proposing organisations. as regards the sharing of contribution between the different partners, you know that the standard community contribution is 50%, and that the other 50% is shared between the member states and the proposing organisations, with the latter paying at least 20%. this sharing of the financial burden between the different partners is based on a very long experience with the promotion programmes. if all partners contribute and become financially involved, the chances for an efficient and well-targeted programme clearly increase. for exceptional cases, such as the recent case of fruit and vegetables for schoolchildren, it is possible to increase the community’s share to 60%. regarding your idea to emphasise more programmes for promotion in third countries, i am, in principle, sympathetic towards the idea, but it has to be put into the right context. this proposal is simply about merging two regulations; it is not about policy discussions or more money, so the right moment to have this discussion would be when we consider the future of our common agricultural policy, where our priorities should be well reflected in our budget allocation. however, this does not mean that i am pushing promotion into the background. as you possibly know, in our two recent reforms – the first on food and vegetables, and the one we will, hopefully, finalise at the beginning of next week, namely the wine reform – we have been focusing and underlining the importance of promoting programmes. to take the example of wine, we have allocated eur 120 million every year specifically for promoting our excellent european wines in third countries. i think we are on the right track, but let us come back to this at a later stage – this is simply a merging of the two regulations.
the rapporteur. madam president! the draft council regulation on the combination of information and promotion measures for agricultural products on the internal market and in third countries is designed to harmonise and consolidate the two regulations currently in force. this is in the wider context of the process of simplifying and making community legislation more transparent. however, i would like to emphasise that simplification is understood here as a technical measure only and the draft regulation in question does not, unfortunately, refer to the essential principles of promotion and information which are described in the implementing rules of the european commission. despite these limitations, my report took a much broader, more strategic approach to the promotion of agricultural products in the european union. the european parliament must be able to address the key issues related to such an important mechanism. in particular, when we take into account the development of multilateral negotiations in the wto and the changes in the conditions for the functioning of the common agricultural policy. all forms of export subsidies, including community export refunds, will be abolished by 2013. the tariff reduction is assumed. in this context, only increased information and promotion activities are able to maintain the export competitiveness of eu agricultural products, to serve the acquisition of new markets in third countries, to increase consumer awareness of the merits of european food and thus to stimulate demand. at the same time, it does not distort competition in the markets and does not affect world trade. we cannot therefore allow the importance of promotion and information activities to be marginalised, but on the contrary, we must make them a priority for the european union. under the current system, the european commission draws up a list of specific products and third countries that can be targeted by campaigns. the list may be revised every two years, while programmes themselves may only be notified once a year, and it is for the european commission to decide whether a programme is approved and what funding it receives. in 2007, the budget for promotion is only €45 million, and it is being reduced every year. this trend is all the more surprising when one considers that both the number of countries in the european union has increased and the general interest in the activities in question has increased significantly. such a policy cannot effectively strengthen the community's position and the recognition of european quality standards, in particular on third country markets. the achievement of such ambitious objectives must be supported by adequate financial means. i therefore believe that the community's financial contribution should be increased from the threshold of 50 to 60% of the actual costs of the programmes. i also propose that the minimum contribution of industry organisations to the funding of programmes be reduced to 10% to give smaller organisations the opportunity to participate. in addition, for organic farming and programmes linked to emergency situations such as avian influenza or bse, the community contribution could be as high as 70%. programmes should be made generally available and more flexible. the inclusion of all products and all countries, as well as the possibility for organisations to submit programmes at least twice a year, will allow for a rapid response to emerging market opportunities and the possibility for producers to expand in third countries. returning to the simplification aspects of the regulation, it was justified to include promotion measures in the single common organisation of agricultural markets regulation, which would increase legislative transparency. it is worth noting that the regulation reforming the fruit and vegetable market and the draft wine reform you mentioned refer to the community promotion instrument. efforts should be made to avoid a situation where the provisions on promotion measures are too fragmented. in conclusion, i would like to take this opportunity to thank the members of the committee on agriculture who unanimously adopted this report, the representatives of the european commission, with whom i have met on several occasions, the 24 agriculture ministers who have written to me on this matter, and the european and national trade organisations for their active cooperation and substantive comments. this consultation enabled me to assess the system in place and to learn about the demands of these countries and organisations and to implement them. in conclusion, i believe that the promotion and information measures, with a correspondingly increased budget, will help european producers and farmers to win new markets and the 'made in europe' brand to be properly identified in the world.
